chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: The Krupa-Cole drum school

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well your school was pretty successful.
Oh yeah, from '54 right on up to '61. But see, around 1960, '59, is when that 'Topsy' got to be a hit. See prior to that, Gene was always busy out on the road,

but he'd be back in you know, and I would be in the school. But when 'Topsy' got to be a hit, I had my quintet that I'd be on the road and Gene on the road; so therefore, hardly ever was both of us in the studio. We had good teachers up there, but people used to come up there and they'd either want Gene or me to teach them or at least to see us every now and then, but by both of us being on the road all the time it was impossible. And so it was impossible to run any kind of business with two bosses away, so that's the reason why we closed it.
Who were some of the students who came out of there? Anybody who later became known?

No, not really because, I don't know, there's a boy, John, Bill Pete, he's a drummer with Jack Teagarden. But he didn't become well known because Jack wasn't featuring drums. He was with Jack Teagarden for a while. Then we had quite a few drummers around there gigging that never got big names.
Between you and having 'Topsy' and I guess the movie of Gene's life came out in the late '50s.
Plus he was in the Benny Goodman story.
